intro.heads_up: Quick heads-up before we dive in: by the time this episode drops Tuesday morning, Orin Straylight's research in Silvermoon is done, if you haven't picked up "Prismatic Potential" yet, go grab it so you can start buying that extra Nebulous Voidcore every week.
rundown: the Forever beta's third week: level 30, a brand-new dungeon, and a 15-versus-15 battleground
Blizzard's class deep dives, and the Rogue and Warrior questions
Tom Ellis logging off X after the name-ban fallout
gold buyers, legacy points, and a hundred-thousand-dollar duel
Aggrend teasing a Blackrock Depths-style mega dungeon
Forever outgrowing its servers while Classic raiders head for the door
everything coming in Midnight's 12.1.5 on October 13, and a look down the road at Wrath Remix
and we'll close out the news with tuning, paid addons in China, the Trading Post, and a little Xbox

items.title: Forever Beta, Week Three: Level 30, the Wetlands, and Darkspear Islands
items.synopsis: The October 1 build pushed the beta to level 30 and opened up a new dungeon, a new battleground, and a pile of tuning that changes how leveling and the economy feel.
points: the level cap going up to 30, with Razorfen Downs and Uldaman now open

points.text: a brand-new dungeon, Excavation Site: Wetlands, for levels 26 to 31
points.sub: Wowhead's note: no Dalaran dungeon this week

points: a new 15-versus-15 battleground on Darkspear Islands
Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, and the Skyborne starting zone all still playable
dungeon quests now giving 50% less bonus XP: Blizzard answering feedback on leveling pace
honor gear costing about 50% more, with the honor cap going from 15,000 to 25,000
skinning back to one skin per mob: the group-wide skinning was a bug
enchanted wands now vendoring for 1 copper, so no more easy money on wand flips
the library book necklaces dropping to uncommon, and the 20-book ring no longer Rogue-only
Stitches showing up neutral in Duskwood: confirmed a bug, he'll be back to terrorizing soon
Ghost Wolf glowing bright blue on purpose for now, because it was invisible in dark zones
more gamepad work: pet stable, compact raid frames, and gamepad bindings now separate from keyboard
questions: Dungeon XP nerfed, skinning fixed, wands worth a copper. Is Blizzard sanding off the fun exploits, or protecting the launch economy?
Where are you parked at level 30, and is the new Wetlands dungeon worth running?

items.title: Forever Classes: Deep Dives, and the Rogue and Warrior Questions
items.synopsis: Blizzard walked through the Forever classes this week, and Rogues and Warriors got the most specific, and most argued-about, answers.
points: 1.12 talent trees with a new 16-point milestone, and talent taxes like Blessing of Kings made baseline
Hunters getting Aimed Shot at 20 and gear-scaling pets; every Priest gets Fear Ward at 20

points.text: Kris Zierhut promising Rogues the highest single-target damage in the game, on a standstill fight
points.sub: "really easy to take them too far": white hits, Slice and Dice, and poisons all stacking

points: the reassurance aimed at PvE Rogues, "not the PvP ones"
Rogue Energy now regenerating continuously, Mutilate hitting with both weapons, and a new Venom finisher
the Gnome racial nerfed twice: Eureka! no longer touches Garrote or Rupture at all

points.text: Warriors' crit Rage going from 75% to 100% after a dual-wield bug threw off Blizzard's tests
points.sub: Aidan Moon confirming it, and Fury getting a whole second pass the same week

points: Fury's tree reshuffled again: Lingering Rage, Furious Precision, Gore Drinker, and Flurry no longer locked behind Enrage
Spearing Strike dismounting players, and Protection reworked as a PvP tech spec for non-shield Warriors
questions: Rogues on top by design: good for Forever, or are raids going to stack them and bench everyone else?
Warriors got reworked mid-week twice: exciting, or a sign the class still isn't settled with a month to launch?

items.title: Tom Ellis Logs Off After the Name-Ban Fallout
items.synopsis: Last week's name bans turned into this week's biggest community story: Forever senior producer Tom Ellis deleted his X account after players went digging through his old posts.
points: Ellis defending the name enforcement: existing legacy ban lists, not Blizzard going "extra woke"

points.text: "I read the list. No sympathy. Be a better human next time."
points.sub: only 0.18% of players removed from beta: the "cheeky name" crowd mostly got forced renames

points: players digging up his posts from around 2009 and 2010 and pushing to get him fired
people tagging Xbox's CEO over a beta character name policy

points.text: Ellis deleting his X account, with reports he cited harassment of friends and family
points.sub: the threats come from his own posts and secondhand reporting, nothing independently confirmed

points: Asmongold calling the "better human" line "fake and patronizing" while saying he'd prefer more "edgy, weird devs"
plenty of players on the forums and Reddit saying the crackdown was refreshing
anecdotal reports some banned testers being let back in with forced renames instead
questions: Should a senior producer be on X arguing with players at all, or was he right to say his piece?
Is fifteen-year-old internet history fair game when someone tells you to be a better human?

items.title: Gold Buyers, Legacy Points, and a $100,000 Duel
items.synopsis: Blizzard is going after gold buyers as well as sellers in Forever, handing every tester 16 Legacy points, and the community already has a six-figure tournament running in the beta.
points: Blizzard actioning beta accounts that botted gold, and accounts that bought or knowingly received it

points.text: a new warning popping up whenever you trade with a stranger
points.sub: "you could put your account at risk of closure"

points: illicit gold removed, suspensions, or permanent closures, for buyers, not just sellers
"knew or should-have-known": be careful taking big gold gifts from people you don't know
all beta testers getting 16 Legacy points in a future week, so the system can actually get tested
Legacy being the alt-friendly prestige layer, and the community mostly loving it

points.text: Tips Out, Esfand, and Xaryu running The Forever Open: a $100,000 dueling tournament on the beta
points.sub: TimTheTatman doubled the prize pool, and 4,000 sign-ups closed registration two days early

questions: Punishing the buyer, not just the seller: fair, or is "should-have-known" going to catch innocent people?
Would either of you ever sign up for a dueling tournament like this?

items.title: Aggrend Teases a Mega Dungeon, and Forever's Dungeon Deep Dive at PAX
items.synopsis: Aggrend hinted that Forever has its own Blackrock Depths waiting at the end, and we may get our first real look at a new dungeon at PAX Aus next week.

points.text: someone asking for "a good BRD-like mega dungeon" and Aggrend replying "Hold our beer(s)."
points.sub: he attached a "spoiler-y" image: Wowhead's read is the endgame dungeon Blackmaw Hold, not confirmed

points: the original Blackrock Depths running about 20 encounters and hours to clear
Clay Stone giving an exclusive deep dive on one of Forever's new dungeons at PAX Aus
Holly Longdale opening PAX with the Storytime keynote, October 8, 6:00 PM Pacific on the Warcraft Twitch
the Dalaran dungeon held back for a future beta build, with Excavation Site: Wetlands out this week
every Forever raid tier getting both a 10-player and a 20-player raid
40-player raids coming back, starting with Onyxia's Lair, but not every tier
questions: Is a three-hour mega dungeon something you'd actually run weekly, or a once-a-month guild night?
BRD was the best dungeon in Classic for a lot of people. Can a new one live up to that?

items.title: Forever Is Eating Classic
items.synopsis: The Forever beta keeps outgrowing its servers, and the raid logs say Classic players are already packing up to move.
points: Holly Longdale: "we had to increase the WoW: Forever Beta population cap again. The wild ride continues."
Blizzard finding and fixing a bug that was filling the login queue

points.text: TBC Anniversary raiders dropping from 212,821 to 124,487 in a single week, about 88,000 gone
points.sub: Ironforge.pro, pulling from Warcraft Logs: Sept 8 to 14 versus Sept 15 to 21, the beta's first week

points: Mists of Pandaria Classic raiders falling from 33,125 to 24,971 in the same stretch
TBC Anniversary still sitting in Black Temple and Hyjal, with Zul'Aman and Sunwell still to come
no word yet on a Wrath Anniversary, or what happens to MoP Classic characters from 2019
Jesse Heinig on Bluesky: a "cultural moment", "we got some juice comin'"
questions: If you're on TBC Anniversary or MoP Classic, are you sticking around, or already gone to Forever?
Should Blizzard say now what happens to the Classic versions, or let Forever launch first?

items.title: Midnight's 12.1.5 Arrives October 13
items.synopsis: The 12.1.5 patch notes are out: a single-boss raid, a nine-chamber Labyrinth, Keystone Myth, and a staggered power ramp starting next week.
points: The Unbinding of Kith'ix: a single-boss raid with Lady Liadrin, and a flexible 15-to-25 Mythic
the C'Thraxxi general that Ula'tek's defeat woke up beneath the Venomous Abyss

points.text: the Labyrinth of Kindo'jan: a nine-chamber, Delve-like mega-dungeon with Valeera Sanguinar
points.sub: Tier 11 solo challenge, Mythic gear, and you can do it one wing at a time

points: Keystone Myth back for Season 2: a 3600 rating for the Venomous Contender title and the Timelost Saddle
an extra Nebulous Voidcore every week from Orin Straylight, starting the week of October 6
Ascendant Venomstones the week of October 20: ten of them push a maxed weapon, trinket, or necklace higher
the crest cap coming off October 20
Aqir Invasions in Eversong or Zul'Aman for ten minutes every hour, with eight possible affixes
player coordinates under the minimap, and Legion and Battle for Azeroth reputations going warband-wide
questions: A single-boss raid with flexible Mythic. Does that work as a mid-season raid, or does it feel thin?
Labyrinth versus Mythic+ for Mythic gear, where are you spending your week?

items.title: The Road Back to Northrend: Wrath of the Lich King Remix
items.category: World of Warcraft: Wrath Remix & The Last Titan
items.synopsis: Wrath Remix lands summer 2027 as the bridge into The Last Titan: Blizzard's own pitch is to see Northrend now, before we go back to it.
points: Wrath of the Lich King Remix as the third Remix, coming summer 2027 right after 12.2.7

points.text: Blizzard's stated reason: lots of players have never been to Northrend, and The Last Titan is going there next
points.sub: read between the lines: a last look at Northrend the way we remember it

points: Blizzard's panel recap telling us to "embrace the power of the Scourge"

points.text: Runeforging for every class: the idea came from Hearthstone art of every class raised by the Scourge
points.sub: think Knights of the Frozen Throne: every hero turned Death Knight

points: my theory: we all fall and come back Scourge, and do Death Knights get to double up on runes?
Scourge Outbreaks out in the world and in dungeons, plus infinitely scaling dungeons
Jake Miller saying it plays closer to Mists Remix, with Wrath being simple enough to leave room for wild new abilities
unreleased items and appearances, and "a modern take" on mounts like Invincible

points.text: The Last Titan as "more than a return to Northrend": Wyrmrest Temple and a colossal figure in the teaser
points.sub: full reveal early 2027, after Eclipse: Blizzard says talking now would spoil Midnight

questions: If Northrend is getting wrecked or rebuilt in The Last Titan, is Remix the goodbye tour, and what would you want to see one more time?
Runeforging on every class. What rune are you putting on your main's weapon?

items.title: Tuning Week and the Race to World First
items.synopsis: Unholy gets brought back down to earth on Tuesday, a handful of underperformers get help, and the top two raiding guilds are talking about fewer splits.
points: Unholy's Blightfall cut in half after a bug fix made it hit way harder than intended
Devourer Demon Hunters getting 8 to 10% single-target buffs across the board
Brewmasters dying too much in dungeons, more Stagger purify and longer dodge windows
Mistweaver healing up 15% to help them in raid
Subtlety's Trickster buffed to close the gap with Deathstalker
Enhancement up 4% across the board, with Lava Lash up 35%
Survival's Wildfire Bomb buff actually landing, and Ula'tek's heart no longer meleeing players

points.text: Liquid and Echo talking about fewer characters and fewer splits for the next Race to World First
points.sub: Echo says it's still in talks: Liquid turned down the first deal over raid-time limits

questions: Is your spec on this list, and does it actually change anything for you on Tuesday?
Would a no-splits race be more fun to watch, or does it just hand the win to whoever has the deeper bench?

items.title: NetEase Cracks Down on Paid Addons in WoW China
items.synopsis: China is enforcing the rule Blizzard's addon policy already has on paper, addons have to be free, and threatening legal action over it.
points: Blizzard's own addon policy, rule one: "Add-ons must be free of charge"
the West living in a grey area: free base addons with paid premium tiers, and streamers selling UI packs to subs

points.text: NetEase banning paid unlocks, VIP tiers, subscriptions, and pay-per-use services on CN realms
points.sub: reported by CN community contributor Elspeth on X

points: even paid WeakAura and config sharing called out
tipping still allowed, as long as it's voluntary and doesn't unlock anything
anyone who keeps selling addons facing legal action
where that leaves my own setup: one personal addon I built for me, never sold
questions: Should Blizzard enforce this in the West too, or would that kill the addons people rely on?
Is selling a UI pack to your subs any different from selling the addon itself?
